content:
Apple is celebrating its 50th anniversary this year, and many users are even older than the company itself. Apple has launched a new support page listing 50 ways to make its devices easier to use, most of which involve accessibility settings.

From adjusting the font size on your Apple Watch to setting your iPhone to notify you when the washing machine finishes, the methods cover a wide range…

Apple says the company's goal is to make its technology accessible to everyone, including the elderly.

At Apple, we believe the best technology should serve everyone, including older adults. That's why our products and services are designed with inclusivity at their core, featuring built-in accessibility features that help you connect, create, and do what you love in the way that suits you best. As you go through different stages of life, the way you interact with the world changes. From enlarging onscreen text to making conversations clearer in a noisy restaurant, Apple's ecosystem of devices, features, and services is designed to adapt to your needs.

The support page mainly lists accessibility features, divided into ten main categories.

  • Vision: See the content on your screen more comfortably
  • Hearing: Stay connected with conversations, alerts, and your surroundings
  • Mobility: Customize how you control and navigate your device
  • Speech: Use your voice in your own way
  • Cognitive: Focus on the present, stay in control
  • Personalization: Create an experience that's uniquely yours
  • Organization: Keep what matters most
  • Health: Stay on top of your health with thoughtful insights
  • Safety: Enjoy peace of mind
  • Communication: Stay connected

Taking the Vision category as an example, it includes options such as enlarging text, bolding text, inverting colors, setting color filters, reducing transparency, increasing contrast, and reducing screen flicker. Some features (such as Sound Recognition), though heavily promoted by Apple when they launched, remain unfamiliar to many users.

Sound Recognition detects specific sounds and uses on-device intelligence to notify you when they're detected. This feature can recognize 15 different sounds—you can also train your device to recognize your own name, as well as unique electronic sounds in your environment, such as the beeping of kitchen appliances, specific types of alarms, or doorbells. On HomePod, Sound Recognition can also detect the sound of smoke or carbon monoxide alarms. Sound Recognition also works with CarPlay. Your iPhone will listen for and identify sirens, horns, and even a baby's cry. When a specific sound is detected, you'll receive a notification—when using CarPlay, the notification will appear on your car's display.

The support page provides a comprehensive overview of the accessibility features currently available across Apple devices, and is packed with content. Each subcategory offers individual guidance for the supported devices. Depending on the feature, this may cover iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV, Vision Pro, and CarPlay.
